vaccines.name: BCG
diseases: Tuberculosis (especially severe forms in young children)
vaccines.purpose: Lowers the chance that a young child develops the most serious forms of tuberculosis, such as TB meningitis.
vaccines.doses_info: Usually one dose, given at birth or as early as possible in the first year.
educational_notes: It protects best against severe childhood TB. It is less reliable at preventing TB of the lungs in adults.
A small scar at the injection site, usually on the upper arm, is normal.
vaccines.technical_description: BCG vaccine provides protection against severe forms of tuberculosis in infants and young children.
vaccines.simple_explanation: The BCG vaccine helps protect young children from the most serious kinds of tuberculosis (TB).

vaccines.name: Hepatitis B
vaccines.purpose: Protects against the hepatitis B virus, which can cause long-term liver infection, liver scarring and liver cancer.
vaccines.doses_info: A birth dose within 24 hours is recommended, followed by further doses. In several schedules the later doses are given inside the pentavalent vaccine.
educational_notes: Hepatitis B can pass from mother to baby during birth, which is why the birth dose is timed so early.
Adults who missed vaccination can usually start a course at any age.
vaccines.technical_description: Hepatitis B vaccine provides protection against hepatitis B virus infection of the liver.
vaccines.simple_explanation: The hepatitis B vaccine helps protect your liver from the hepatitis B virus.

vaccines.name: Oral polio vaccine (OPV)
vaccines.purpose: Protects children against polio, a virus that can cause permanent paralysis.
vaccines.doses_info: Several doses over the first years of life. Some programmes add a dose at birth (often written OPV-0) and a booster in the second year.
educational_notes: It is given as drops by mouth.
Polio campaign doses (such as pulse polio days) are extra and may not be counted as routine doses.
vaccines.technical_description: Oral polio vaccine provides protection against poliovirus, which can cause paralysis.
vaccines.simple_explanation: The oral polio vaccine, given as drops, helps protect children from polio, an infection that can cause paralysis.

vaccines.name: Inactivated polio vaccine (IPV / fIPV)
vaccines.purpose: An injected polio vaccine that adds to the protection from oral polio drops.
vaccines.doses_info: Schedules differ. India's programme uses a fractional dose (fIPV) given into the skin.
educational_notes: IPV cannot cause vaccine-derived polio, which is one reason it is used alongside or after oral doses.
vaccines.technical_description: Inactivated polio vaccine provides protection against poliovirus and cannot itself cause polio.
vaccines.simple_explanation: The injected polio vaccine helps protect children from polio and cannot cause the disease.

vaccines.name: DTP (DPT / DTwP)
vaccines.purpose: Protects against three serious bacterial infections that can affect breathing, nerves and muscles.
vaccines.doses_info: A primary series in infancy, then boosters in the second year and again around school age. Programmes that use pentavalent give the primary doses in that vaccine.
educational_notes: Protection fades over time, which is why boosters are scheduled.
A mild fever or sore arm for a day or two is common.
vaccines.technical_description: DTP vaccine provides protection against diphtheria, tetanus and pertussis.
vaccines.simple_explanation: The DTP vaccine helps protect against three infections: diphtheria, tetanus and whooping cough.

vaccines.name: Pentavalent (DPT-HepB-Hib)
vaccines.purpose: Combines five vaccines in a single injection so infants need fewer pricks.
vaccines.doses_info: Three doses in infancy in India's programme, usually at 6, 10 and 14 weeks.
educational_notes: Hib can cause meningitis and pneumonia in young children.
vaccines.technical_description: Pentavalent vaccine provides protection against diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis, hepatitis B and Haemophilus influenzae type b.
vaccines.simple_explanation: The pentavalent vaccine helps protect babies against five infections: diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, hepatitis B and Hib.

vaccines.name: Rotavirus vaccine
vaccines.purpose: Lowers the risk of severe, dehydrating diarrhoea in babies.
vaccines.doses_info: Two or three oral doses in infancy depending on the product and programme. It has an upper age limit, so timing matters.
educational_notes: It is given as drops by mouth.
It should not be started late in infancy, so check with a provider if doses were delayed.
vaccines.technical_description: Rotavirus vaccine provides protection against severe gastroenteritis caused by rotavirus in infants.
vaccines.simple_explanation: The rotavirus vaccine helps protect babies from the stomach infection that most often causes severe diarrhoea.

vaccines.name: Pneumococcal conjugate (PCV)
diseases: Pneumonia, meningitis and bloodstream infection caused by pneumococcus
vaccines.purpose: Protects young children against serious infections caused by pneumococcal bacteria.
vaccines.doses_info: Two or three doses in infancy and a booster around 9 to 15 months, depending on the schedule.
educational_notes: Older children and adults at higher risk may use different pneumococcal vaccines.
vaccines.technical_description: Pneumococcal conjugate vaccine provides protection against invasive disease caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae.
vaccines.simple_explanation: The pneumococcal vaccine helps protect children from pneumonia, meningitis and blood infections caused by pneumococcus bacteria.

vaccines.name: Measles-Rubella (MR)
vaccines.purpose: Protects against measles, which can cause pneumonia and brain swelling, and rubella, which can harm an unborn baby.
vaccines.doses_info: Two doses: the first around 9 to 12 months and the second in the second year of life.
educational_notes: Two doses are needed for strong, lasting protection.
Rubella protection matters for future pregnancies.
vaccines.technical_description: Measles-rubella vaccine provides protection against measles and rubella.
vaccines.simple_explanation: The MR vaccine helps protect you against two infections: measles and rubella.

vaccines.name: MMR
vaccines.purpose: Protects against measles, mumps and rubella in one vaccine.
vaccines.doses_info: Usually two doses in childhood. It can count towards the measles and rubella doses of a schedule.
educational_notes: Private paediatric schedules in India often use MMR in place of MR.
vaccines.technical_description: The MMR vaccine provides protection against measles, mumps, and rubella.
vaccines.simple_explanation: The MMR vaccine helps protect you against three infections: measles, mumps, and rubella.

sources.name: Indian Academy of Pediatrics - immunization schedule

vaccines.name: Japanese encephalitis (JE)
diseases: Japanese encephalitis (a brain infection spread by mosquitoes)
vaccines.purpose: Protects against a mosquito-borne brain infection found in parts of Asia.
vaccines.doses_info: In India, two doses are given in districts where the disease is common, around 9 to 12 months and 16 to 24 months.
educational_notes: It is offered only in areas where Japanese encephalitis is a known risk, so it may not apply to everyone.
vaccines.technical_description: Japanese encephalitis vaccine provides protection against Japanese encephalitis virus.
vaccines.simple_explanation: The JE vaccine helps protect against a brain infection that mosquitoes can spread in some regions.

vaccines.name: Td (tetanus-diphtheria)
vaccines.purpose: A booster that renews protection against tetanus and diphtheria for older children, adolescents and adults.
vaccines.doses_info: India's programme gives Td at 10 and 16 years, and during pregnancy. WHO recommends a booster in adolescence.
educational_notes: Td replaced the older tetanus toxoid (TT) vaccine in India's schedule.
vaccines.technical_description: Td vaccine provides protection against tetanus and diphtheria.
vaccines.simple_explanation: The Td vaccine is a booster that helps protect you against tetanus and diphtheria.

vaccines.name: Tetanus toxoid (TT)
vaccines.purpose: An older tetanus-only vaccine that appears on many earlier records.
vaccines.doses_info: Replaced by Td in India's national schedule. A TT entry on an older card is still a valid record of a tetanus dose.
educational_notes: VaxTrack stores TT separately from Td. It is shown in your history but not matched to the Td schedule items.
vaccines.technical_description: Tetanus toxoid vaccine provides protection against tetanus.
vaccines.simple_explanation: The tetanus toxoid vaccine helps protect you from tetanus.

vaccines.name: Tdap
vaccines.purpose: A booster that adds whooping cough protection to the tetanus and diphtheria booster.
vaccines.doses_info: Often used in adolescence and in each pregnancy, according to national advice.
educational_notes: Your local health authority decides who should receive it and when.
vaccines.technical_description: Tdap vaccine provides protection against tetanus, diphtheria and acellular pertussis.
vaccines.simple_explanation: The Tdap vaccine helps protect you against three infections: tetanus, diphtheria and whooping cough.

vaccines.name: HPV
diseases: Cervical cancer and other cancers caused by human papillomavirus
vaccines.purpose: Protects against the HPV types that cause most cervical cancers.
vaccines.doses_info: WHO recommends one or two doses for girls aged 9 to 14. Older starters may need three doses.
educational_notes: The vaccine works best when given before any exposure to the virus.
Check your national programme, since eligibility and doses vary by country.
vaccines.technical_description: HPV vaccine provides protection against infection with the human papillomavirus types that cause cervical cancer.
vaccines.simple_explanation: The HPV vaccine helps protect against the virus that causes most cervical cancers.

vaccines.name: Typhoid conjugate (TCV)
vaccines.purpose: Protects against typhoid fever, which spreads through contaminated food and water.
vaccines.doses_info: A single dose from about 6 months of age in many private schedules. Not part of every national programme.
educational_notes: Older typhoid vaccines needed repeat doses every few years, so ask which type you received.
vaccines.technical_description: Typhoid conjugate vaccine provides protection against Salmonella Typhi, the bacterium that causes typhoid fever.
vaccines.simple_explanation: The typhoid vaccine helps protect you from typhoid fever.

vaccines.name: Hepatitis A
diseases: Hepatitis A (a viral liver infection spread through food and water)
vaccines.purpose: Protects against hepatitis A, which causes liver inflammation and can make people ill for weeks.
vaccines.doses_info: Usually one or two doses depending on the product.
educational_notes: It is common in paediatric private schedules and for travellers to some regions.
vaccines.technical_description: Hepatitis A vaccine provides protection against hepatitis A virus.
vaccines.simple_explanation: The hepatitis A vaccine helps protect your liver from the hepatitis A virus.

vaccines.name: Varicella (chickenpox)
vaccines.purpose: Lowers the chance of chickenpox and its complications.
vaccines.doses_info: Two doses in many schedules, a few months to a few years apart.
educational_notes: Not part of India's national programme; it is commonly given in private practice.
vaccines.technical_description: Varicella vaccine provides protection against varicella-zoster virus infection.
vaccines.simple_explanation: The varicella vaccine helps protect you from chickenpox.

vaccines.name: Influenza (flu)
vaccines.purpose: Lowers the risk of seasonal flu and serious flu complications.
vaccines.doses_info: Offered every year because flu viruses change. Children getting it for the first time may need two doses.
educational_notes: Each season's vaccine is updated to match circulating strains.
vaccines.technical_description: Seasonal influenza vaccine provides protection against circulating influenza viruses.
vaccines.simple_explanation: The flu vaccine helps protect you from seasonal influenza.

vaccines.name: COVID-19
vaccines.purpose: Lowers the risk of severe COVID-19 illness.
vaccines.doses_info: Recommendations have changed several times. Cards often list the brand name, dose number and a batch number.
educational_notes: Brand names such as Covishield and Covaxin are recognised and filed under COVID-19.
vaccines.technical_description: COVID-19 vaccines provide protection against severe disease caused by SARS-CoV-2.
vaccines.simple_explanation: COVID-19 vaccines help protect you from becoming seriously ill with COVID-19.
